text:
incident-bot: Pager: High p99 latency detected on /v1/chat/completions (chat-prod). Group: chat-ingress. Triggered 2135056789. Severity: P99 spike -> automatic page. Link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/2135056789 :rotating_light:

maria: I’m seeing the spike correlated with requests hitting model=mistral-1 and route=/chat/assistant. p99 jumped to ~2.4s for the last 3m. Customers A/C have a few errors but most are just slow.

ajay: grabbing logs. can someone check if we have unusual payload sizes or a batch/queue backlog?

sophie: looking at the dashboard now — requests count is normal but KV-cache hit rate dropped ~40% at the same time. could be cache invalidation from a deploy?

chris: no deploys in the last 6h from deploy-bot. infra metrics show GPU utilization steady. network egress small spike in one AZ.

maria: ok. two things: 1) immediate mitigation plan; 2) post-incident alert tuning so we don’t page on noisy short-lived blips.

leo: for immediate mitigation we can: 
- ripple traffic off mistral-1 to mistral-1-quant (slightly lower perf but more stable) for 30m
- increase dedicated pool for chat-prod by 1 node (if capacity available)
Which do folks prefer?

ajay: fallback to mistral-1-quant for new requests + keep in-flight to finish sounds safest. I’ll open the rapid rollback route.

maria: please do that, @ajay. I’ll apply a temporary alert squelch so on-call doesn’t keep paging while we confirm mitigation.

incident-bot: Note: applying manual pager_squelch by maria until 2135057300 (10m).

sophie: re: alerting, current policy is pretty blunt: p99 > 1200ms for 3m -> page. That captures a lot of noise for chat routes that naturally fluctuate. Proposal below.

maria: paste proposal pls.

sophie: proposal (short):
- Introduce per-route baselines and only page if p99 exceeds baseline * 1.6 OR absolute 1500ms, whichever higher.
- Add a noise gate: require request count >= 50 in window OR delta > 30% sustained across two windows (5m each).
- Move to two-tier alerting: 5m p99>threshold -> non-pager ticket (ops) + 15m sustained -> pager.
- Make the rule model-aware: tag by model.family (mistral, llama, etc.) so we can target the worst offenders.

ajay: +1. sample alert config (pseudo):
```yaml
alert_name: chat.p99.route
filters:
  - route: "/v1/chat/completions"
  - env: prod
group_by: [route, model.family]
conditions:
  - window: 5m
    threshold: "max(baseline(route,model.family)*1.6, 1500)"
    min_count: 50
    noise_gate: "delta(5m, prev=5m) > 0.3"
escalation:
  - 5m: create ticket (no page)
  - 15m: pager
```
chris: one caveat — baseline generation needs a stable period. if we roll new models frequently, baselines can be stale. we should fall back to a global per-route baseline if model.family baseline is under-sampled.

leo: agree. Also we need a dashboard that surfaces per-model latency + request volume + cache hit rate side-by-side so oncall can quickly see reason for spike.

sophie: I sketched a dashboard layout: 
- row1: per-route p50/p95/p99 heatmap by model.family (last 6h)
- row2: request rate + KV-cache hit % timeseries per route
- row3: synthetic-slo probe latency (from 3 regions)
- row4: alert history overlay with annotations for deploys and config changes
We can reuse existing widgets.

maria: for immediate action items: 
- @ajay: kickoff route fallback to mistral-1-quant now, post link to runbook when done.
- @leo: if fallback insufficient, request +1 pool from infra and PM to accept short burst costs.
- @sophie: create the per-route/model dashboard draft and shared query snippets.
- @chris: implement baseline fallback logic (route-level default) in alerting engine.
- @maria: update incident channel with customer impact summary after 30m.

ajay: starting fallback now — command I ran: 
```bash
redwood route update --route /v1/chat/completions --fallback-model mistral-1-quant --drain-inflight true
```
link: https://ops.redwood/run/7890

incident-bot: Automation: route update triggered by ajay. status: in_progress.

leo: we didn’t get many error responses, mainly latency. I’m going to open a quick support note for top 3 customers that had highest p99, cc: @maria.

maria: thanks. initial customer impact: minor degradation for ~12 customers (mainly bulk chat integrations). No SLO breach yet but heads-up to biz. I’ll write a one-paragraph update for CSMs.

sophie: on the longer-term alert tuning side, I want to run a backtest over the last 90 days to compute per-route/model baselines and false-positive rate if we apply the new rules. Will need a job and a PR with data. Target: EOW.

chris: also record a canary window change: we'll test the new two-tier escalation on a single non-critical route for two weeks before rolling to all chat routes.

maria: handoff: I need to step away in ~10m. @ajay you’ll own the oncall until 2135057300. please monitor the squelch expiry and escalate if p99 doesn’t drop under threshold after fallback.

ajay: got it. I’ll watch p99 and reroute back if we see regression. I’ll also open the ticket for tuning and tag team leads.

leo: quick note for postmortem: include timeline (cache drop -> latency spike -> fallback -> recovery), config diffs around cache TTLs, any infra blips in that AZ, and list of alert policy changes proposed.

maria: perfect. thanks team. I’ll post the customer note in #customer-impact and escalate to CSM if any customer reports.

incident-bot: Pager cleared at 2135056895 by ajay. Manual squelch removed.

ajay: closing thread — followups created: OPS-4321 (alert backtest), OPS-4322 (dashboard), OPS-4323 (baseline fallback).

maria: handing to @ajay for monitoring during his shift. :thumbsup:
